title: Implement async eval-run invocation service (job runner) for Optimize gating
creator: Jordan Lee
description:
Background
Optimize can propose cost-saving config changes (batching/caching/quantization/routing) that must be gated by quality evals before apply. This ticket builds the async eval-run invocation service that executes those evals reliably and returns a structured gating summary.

Scope
- Add a control-plane service/module: "eval-runner" (async job runner) responsible for:
  - Accepting a gating eval request from Optimize apply flow (UI and API path).
  - Enqueuing jobs with concurrency limits and per-tenant fairness.
  - Invoking eval-harness in "gating mode" with deterministic inputs.
  - Persisting run state + summary + artifact pointers.
  - Retrying transient failures; enforcing timeouts/cancellation.
  - Returning a stable run_id for later polling and audit logging.

Non-goals
- Designing thresholds/policy evaluation logic (handled by policy engine + schema work).
- Replacing eval-harness; we call it.

Design / approach
Job model
- Create EvalRun records keyed by a server-generated run_id (ULID) with fields:
  - tenant_id, project_id (if available), route_id, model_id, model_version
  - prompt_set_revision, suite_id(s), optimization_type, config_delta_hash
  - requested_by (actor), requested_at
  - status: QUEUED | RUNNING | SUCCEEDED | FAILED | TIMED_OUT | CANCELED
  - attempt_count, last_error_class, last_error_message (redacted)
  - timing: queue_latency_ms, runtime_ms, total_elapsed_ms
  - result_summary_json (small; capped) and artifact_uri(s) (S3/GCS depending on env)
  - idempotency_key (optional; used by Optimize apply endpoint to de-dupe)

Queue + workers
- Use the existing control-plane job queue primitives (same as backfills), but add:
  - Per-tenant max in-flight gating jobs (default 2; configurable).
  - Global worker concurrency cap (default 50 in hosted control plane; lower in staging).
  - Priority lanes: P0 for apply-gating (interactive), P2 for backfills (ENG-3923).
  - Jittered exponential backoff for retries.

Retries / error handling
- Retry policy:
  - Retryable: transient network errors, 5xx from eval-harness service, worker preemption, artifact store transient failures.
  - Non-retryable: invalid request schema, missing prompt set revision, permission denied, eval-harness returns deterministic "invalid suite" errors.
  - Default: up to 2 retries (3 total attempts), backoff 30s / 2m (+ jitter).
- Timeout policy:
  - Hard timeout per run: 15 minutes (apply-gating) initially.
  - Soft timeout: 10 minutes -> mark as at risk and emit telemetry.
  - If run times out: status TIMED_OUT; persist partial logs/artifacts if available.

Invocation contract with eval-harness
- Call eval-harness with:
  - model identifier + exact model version
  - prompt set revision(s)
  - suite selector output (list of suites) and workload tags
  - config under test (the candidate Optimize config) + baseline config for comparison
  - gating mode flag to ensure output format contains:
    - aggregated metrics + confidence intervals
    - prompt_set_revision metadata
    - suite version + harness build sha
- Store the full raw eval output as an artifact; store only a compact summary inline for quick rendering/audit events.

Result persistence + API
- Persist EvalRun summary for:
  - Optimize apply UI (polling, show progress, show failure reasons)
  - audit logging (OptimizeConfigChange event references run_id)
  - dashboards/alerts (pass/fail/timeouts, latency, backlog)
- API endpoints (internal control plane):
  - POST /internal/guardrails/eval-runs (create, returns run_id; accepts idempotency_key)
  - GET /internal/guardrails/eval-runs/{run_id} (status + summary + artifact links)
  - POST /internal/guardrails/eval-runs/{run_id}:cancel (best-effort)
  - POST /internal/guardrails/eval-runs/{run_id}:replay (admin-only; used for debugging)

Telemetry
- Emit metrics:
  - guardrails_eval_runs_created_total (by tenant_tier, optimization_type)
  - guardrails_eval_runs_inflight (by lane)
  - guardrails_eval_run_queue_latency_ms p50/p95
  - guardrails_eval_run_runtime_ms p50/p95
  - guardrails_eval_run_total_latency_ms p50/p95
  - guardrails_eval_run_attempts (distribution)
  - guardrails_eval_run_failures_total (by error_class)
  - guardrails_eval_run_timeouts_total
- Add structured logs with run_id and tenant_id; ensure prompt content never logged.

Operational considerations
- Rate limits to avoid overwhelming eval-harness or GPU pools.
- Ensure eval traffic is isolated from customer inference traffic (separate worker pool / routing) per SRE guidance.
- Provide admin tooling hooks (later ticket ENG-18612) to inspect backlog and replay runs.

Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Optimize apply flow can create an eval run and receives a run_id immediately (no long synchronous blocking).
- [ ] Worker executes eval-harness call, persists status transitions, and writes artifacts.
- [ ] Retries occur only for retryable classes; attempts count visible in run summary.
- [ ] Timeouts correctly transition to TIMED_OUT and surface to caller.
- [ ] Concurrency limits prevent runaway job creation; per-tenant fairness validated in load test.
- [ ] GET endpoint returns deterministic, schema-validated summary suitable for UI + audit logs.
- [ ] Metrics emitted and visible in staging dashboards; error logs are redacted and do not contain prompt text.

Test plan
- Unit tests for retry classifier and timeout handling.
- Integration test in staging with mocked eval-harness:
  - success, transient failure -> retry -> success
  - non-retryable failure -> FAILED
  - timeout -> TIMED_OUT
  - cancel -> CANCELED (best-effort)
- Load test: 100 tenants * 5 runs each; verify per-tenant in-flight caps.

Rollout plan
- Stage behind feature flag: guardrails.eval_runner.enabled
  - Observe-only first (create runs but don’t block apply) via ENG-3913 gating integration.
  - Enable for internal canary tenants; then design partners.

Open questions
- Default timeout: do we need a shorter interactive budget for Console (e.g., 5–8 min) with background completion? (SRE prefers hard cap; PM wants fewer "timeout" UX states.)
- Artifact retention: confirm retention window and size limits (see data retention ticket/PR).
- Idempotency semantics: should key be (tenant, route, model_version, config_delta_hash, prompt_set_rev, suite list) or only per apply attempt?
